findings.summary: The CLI audit surface and the README omit the most security-relevant consequence of a TLS-pinning passthrough: izba stops verifying the upstream certificate. `izba policy show pin2` printed '⚠ :443 protocol: tcp — pinning passthrough: spliced opaquely; no L7 rules, no request audit, no credential injection' (shard 0 / smoke-declare-pinned-port-accepted / action[2], reproduced independently in state_evidence.per_sandbox.pin2.policy_show), and README.md:88-89 says only 'spliced opaquely — no L7 rules, no request audit.' The only user-facing string in the product naming the loss is the desktop app (app/src/components/PolicyEditor.tsx:106). In its place the CLI advertises 'no credential injection', which does not ship until M5 P2. Predicted flag D1; confirmed at artifact level (the rendered line + the fair-test surface), not by the actor, which never reached the docs. Fix: crates/izba-cli/src/commands/policy.rs live Some(Protocol::Tcp) branch + README.md:88-89; the verbatim string assertions at policy.rs:1166 and policy.rs:1217 must be updated in the same edit. Relates to issue #239 AC-2 (GUI must match the CLI 'in substance'); no existing open issue covers it.

findings.summary: The functional oracle scored a plain shell command that never touched the product as a product failure: graded_cmd 'cat ../../README.md' exited 1 ('No such file or directory') in shard 0 / smoke-docs-find-pinning-exception / action[8], because the step carried no expect_cmd_re and the step's last action was graded. Restrict the functional oracle to actions invoking the izba binary, or prefer the last izba-invoking action of the step. Files: hack/dogfood/oracles.py, hack/dogfood/run_journeys.py.
findings.anchor: hack/dogfood/oracles.py::functional_oracle — 'a deliberately WEAK proposer, not an outcome verdict'

findings.summary: 2 of 3 docs-only journeys produced zero usable evidence. smoke-docs-bare-port-is-inspected emitted NO actions (unreached_decisive, not budget exhaustion — the next journey in the same shard ran fine), and smoke-docs-find-pinning-exception spent 8 of 9 actions catting files that cannot exist in the scratch workdir (README.md, ../README.md, ../../README.md, CLAUDE.md, docs/design-lineage.md) even though the README text was already in its own context pack (context-pack.md:6,84-91). A docs journey needs an explicit answer action graded by a text hook, or compilation into --help probes only, plus one line in context-pack.md stating there is no repo checkout in the workspace. Files: hack/dogfood/run_journeys.py (_grade_decisive_from_observed), the journey compiler, context-pack.md.

smoke-manifest-egress-review-available reached its core expectation through a path that bypasses the feature under test. 'izba create --name pin3 .' (action[1]) consumed the folder's izba.yml (stderr 'resolving alpine:3.20' — the manifest's image), so the sandbox was born in sync: 'izba diff' printed 'state: in sync / no field changes' three times (actions[2],[3],[4]) although step 1 expected a pending change, and 'izba promote .' (action[5]) was a no-op that still printed 'promoted pin3'. The graded core step then passed on 'izba policy show pin3' showing example.com [80,443] — a host put there by create, not by diff→promote. Capability manifest-egress-review is NOT established; 4 downstream journeys require it. Tighten: create the sandbox without the manifest (or with a differing egress block) so diff must render a pending egress change. Files: dogfood-passthrough/tier-smoke.json, dogfood-passthrough/journeys.json.
